newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up on short covering.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up on short covering.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended higher across the board Monday in an active session, with the complex underpinned by short covering despite some weakness in the cash, market sources said.
August climbed 3.7 cents to close at $2.183 per million British thermal units. September settled 5.5 cents higher at $2.151. Other deferreds ended up by one to 4.3 cents.

"When August held support in the $2.125 area, we got a lot of short covering, and there was some heavy fund buying in September too," one Midwest trader said, adding a cold front spilling into the Midwest and East this week could pressure physical and paper prices near-term.

Despite some heat today in the East, Weather Services Corp expects temperatures there to cool tonight and remain below-normal for most of the week. Cooler Midwest weather also is forecast for the week, with Texas temperatures expected to drift around normal for the period.

Chart traders said August remained in a technical range, with support at $2.07 and then at the $2.051 low from July 8. Major trendline resistance was pegged at about $2.20. Further selling was likely at the $2.29 and $2.36 prominent highs.

But with August set to expire Tuesday, traders turned their attention to September, where support was pegged at last week's low of $2.045. Resistance was seen first along the down trendline in the high-teens and then at $2.20.

In the cash Monday, Gulf Coast prices slipped several cents to the mid-teens, with gas at the Hub quoted in the high-teens. Midcon pipes were down a nickel at about the $2.10 level. New York city gate gas was flat to up slightly at $2.40-2.41.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip fell 2.7 cents to $2.221. NYMEX said 77,169 contracts traded, more than double Friday's revised tally of 35,473.

On the KCBT, August finished up 1.5 cents at $2.11, while deferreds ended one to 4.5 cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 2.2 cents to 7.3 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 320 contracts traded, down from Friday's total of 475.
KCBT August natgas futures expire Wednesday, July 30.
